title: An explicit n-minus-one-parameter family of local isometric deformations of a complex quadric with distinct nonzero axes into complex dimension two n minus one shares spherical conjugate coordinates and generically nondegenerate joined second fundamental forms for n at least three
author: Ion I. Dincă
source_title: Peterson's Deformations of Higher Dimensional Quadrics
difficulty_reason: Preserving a quadric metric in higher codimension requires the different rotating coordinate pairs to satisfy all mixed metric terms simultaneously. The author designs the telescoping separated radii and angular quadratures, then verifies the common conjugate-coordinate equations and computes the independent normal fields. A displayed joint-normal determinant establishes generic nondegeneracy of this constructed family.

proof_review.note: Select the direct local construction of Theorem1, with n>=3, pairwise distinct nonzero complex axes and the spherical coordinate chart. Read all Sections2-4 physical4-9: separated metric equations, telescoping radius identities, phase and final-coordinate quadratures, mixed-derivative conjugacy, explicit normal fields/second forms and the generic joint-normal determinant. The source explicitly assumes local open domains on which the functions and required inverses are analytic/nonzero, and accounts for square-root sign choices by principal-plane symmetries; that local scope is preserved. Routine final determinant evaluation follows the full displayed matrix, rather than replacing a missing construction. Petersons original two-dimensional example and Gauss-Weingarten conventions are background; the arbitrary-dimensional constructed family is authored here. No maximality/classification theorem, global branch continuation or totally real form classification is counted. Later Theorem2 normal-completion sign conventions are unreviewed for admission and are not used by the direct Theorem1 proof. Exact selected statement and terminal proof pages rendered and visually inspected; physical headers/native ZIP members and source/license hashes checked. No independent mathematical reproof.

statement_scope: The direct local regular analytic-branch construction of Theorem1 for n>=3 and a_0,...,a_n pairwise distinct nonzero complex axes, with complex Euclidean bilinear metric. Original formulas(1) construct X_z in C^(2n-1) for z in C^(n-1) on the stated domains of validity, with |dX_z|^2=|dX|^2 and the spherical coordinates a common conjugate system. Joined second forms are nondegenerate on the source generic open dense parameter/coordinate set. No maximality, unrestricted global branch or real-surface classification assertion selected.
